criteria.reason: The student provided a clear definition of a data structure, explaining its purpose and importance in computer science.
The student correctly identified the two main categories of data structures: primitive and non-primitive. They also provided examples for each category.
The student provided examples of primitive data structures (int, float, char, boolean, string) and non-linear data structures (Tree, Graph, Hash Table).
The student explained the characteristics of non-linear data structures, including their hierarchical or networked relationships, and provided examples (Tree, Graph, Hash Table).
The student answer provides a clear definition of an algorithm.
The student answer lists all the characteristics of a good algorithm: input, output, definiteness, finiteness, effectiveness, and correctness.
The student answer does not provide specific examples of the characteristics of a good algorithm.
The student answer does not explain deterministic behaviour.
The student provided a clear definition of complexity analysis, which is a technique to evaluate how an algorithm's time and space requirements grow as the input size increases.
The student listed two types of complexity analysis: time complexity and space complexity, which is a good start.
The student only mentioned time complexity, but did not provide examples of O(1), O(n), or O(n^2).
The student did not provide an example of space complexity, which is a crucial part of the types of complexity analysis.
The student correctly defined an array as a linear data structure that stores a fixed-size, sequential collection of elements of the same data types in contiguous memory locations.
The student correctly defined a linked list as a linear data structure consisting of a sequence of nodes, where each node contains data and a reference to the next node.
The student correctly identified that linked lists have elements stored in non-contiguous memory locations and are connected through pointers.
The student correctly stated that arrays have a fixed size.
The student correctly identified that linked lists have dynamic growth.
